source_document.body:
Photographer Hreinn Hjartarson
Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.
Vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads. And Iceland’s windiest months coincide with the time of year when less water flows into its reservoirs.
Landsvirkjun , Iceland’s national power company, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026. The first 14 turbines are online; another 14 will be installed in a second phase, and the entire wind farm is expected to be operating by the end of 2027.
Once complete, Vaðölduver will have 120 megawatts (MW) of capacity. When I met with the folks at Landsvirkjun in Reykjavik last month, they told me that’s enough to power the equivalent of 90,000 Icelandic households. Vaðalda’s electricity feeds into the grid and is sold through power purchase agreements.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
More wind, less pressure on water
Photographer Hreinn Hjartarson
Vaðölduver sits on a lava-and-sand plain east of the Þjórsá River, south of Sultartangi Dam. Landsvirkjun already operates seven hydropower stations in the surrounding Þjórsá and Tungnaá region.
The wind farm was sited in this region of Iceland because the seasons line up nicely.
The winds are strongest in winter, when inflows into hydropower reservoirs can be low. In summer, wind speeds tend to drop, but glacial melt increases water availability for the hydropower system.
When the wind turbines are generating plenty of electricity, Landsvirkjun can ease off hydropower and leave more water in its reservoirs. When the wind drops, hydropower can pick up more of the demand.
That gives the utility more control over when it uses its stored water and helps that water go further.
Plenty of wind closer to the ground
German wind turbine maker Enercon manufactured Vaðölduver’s turbines. The project also includes a service and maintenance agreement with Enercon.
Landsvirkjun had a decade of experience operating pilot wind turbines before building Vaðölduver. One big thing they learned: They didn’t need tall towers to find plenty of wind.
There’s little vegetation or other surface obstructions across this unique, exposed landscape. That allows the turbines to capture productive winds closer to the ground than they could at a more wooded or sheltered location.
“Lower” is relative, of course. The turbines still reach 150 meters (492 feet) at their highest blade tip.
The wind farm covers 17.1 square kilometers (6.6 square miles). Twenty-five turbines are rated at 4.26 MW each, and the remaining three at 4.5 MW. Landsvirkjun’s presentation puts annual generation at 440 GWh and lists a P50 net efficiency figure of 43%, which is considered strong for onshore wind.
A third pillar for Iceland’s power supply
The ability to tap into existing infrastructure was a major factor in Landsvirkjun’s site selection. Where a wind farm goes affects its cost, its environmental footprint, and the people who live nearby.
Landsvirkjun also identifies active engagement with communities and other stakeholders as essential to building wind projects. At Vaðölduver, the immediate task is to finish the remaining 14 turbines while the first phase completes its trial runs.
The company sees wind as a potential third pillar of Iceland’s electricity supply alongside hydropower and geothermal. Vaðölduver shows how those resources can work together, with wind adding generation while helping conserve stored water.
Electrek’s Take
Iceland is a world leader in clean energy. It generates nearly 100% of its electricity from renewable sources, combining hydropower fueled by glacial runoff and rivers (around 70%) and geothermal energy (around 30%).
Over 90% of Icelandic households use direct geothermal hot water for space heating and hot water, while the remaining homes use renewable electricity.
But it’s got the same grid capacity challenges as every other country. Adding wind – and anything else that uses power – means paying close attention to what the grid can handle. Iceland has an isolated transmission system, so maintaining stability and ensuring sufficient capacity are increasingly important as the country develops more projects.
While in Reykjavik, I met with the Minister of the Environment, Energy and Climate, Jóhann Páll Jóhannsson, who told me that the Icelandic grid’s capacity is expected to grow from 20 TWh to 24-25 TWh within a decade. Jóhannsson also said that he is pro-data center and that investors are keen to establish more of them in the country.
When I asked Jóhannsson and his team, as well as the teams at Landsvirkjun and publicly owned ON Power, Iceland’s second-largest electricity generator and largest EV charger network, about grid expansion plans to handle that pipeline, they all said that legislative reforms were being passed to speed up energy permitting processes. There is also financing in place to grow the grid. The physical transmission network is being expanded, but the process is slow because NIMBYism is creating bottlenecks.
In learning about new and completed Icelandic power projects during my visit, it was apparent that the companies in the power and geothermal heat sector regularly collaborate on projects – everyone brings their expertise to the table and works for the common good (yes, really).
But what was striking in discussions about grid expansion was that there seemed to be no plans to pitch in with the Icelandic transmission system operator (TSO), Landsnet hf. It seemed that the plan was to let the TSO come up with the solutions on its own. At most, Jóhannsson’s team said its legislative reform “opened the door” to possible grid innovations.
When I asked the Landsvirkjun team whether they were considering working with the TSO on distributed energy resource (DER) projects like virtual power plants and onsite battery storage for its heavy-industry clients, which make up 80% of its business, they said they hadn’t considered it.
Iceland has earned its reputation as a clean energy leader. Bringing that same collaborative and creative approach to expanding its grid would help it keep setting an example for the rest of the world.

Stanley Druckenmiller. ( Screenshot from Bloomberg TV | YouTube. )
By: Staff Writer November 17, 2026
Billionaire investor Stanley Druckenmiller said Tuesday he was betting on a drop in copper prices, a day after his family office disclosed new stakes in three gold producers. The shares were worth $129.1 million (C$184.6 million) at Sept. 30 closing prices.
Duquesne Family Office held 380,400 shares of Newmont (NYSE, ASX: NEM) worth $43.9 million, 1,054,600 shares of Barrick Mining (TSX: ABX; NYSE: B) worth $42.9 million and 231,050 shares of Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX, NYSE: AEM) worth $42.3 million, according to its quarterly filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Druckenmiller described his copper short at the TomorrowX investment conference in Austin, Texas, where he said his priority was preserving capital , Barron’s reported. He cautioned that the U.S. economy could disappoint in the second half of 2027, CoinDesk reported.
The three gold producers accounted for 2.9% of the $4.5 billion in securities Duquesne disclosed at the end of September. Three industrial-metals holdings worth a combined $70.7 million at the end of June had dropped off its filing.
Southern Copper, Cliffs
Duquesne’s June filing listed 123,060 shares of Southern Copper (NYSE: SCCO) worth $21.4 million, 4.2 million shares of steelmaker Cleveland-Cliffs (NYSE: CLF) worth $39.6 million and 185,640 shares of aluminum producer Alcoa (NYSE: AA) worth $9.7 million.
Duquesne kept its 300,200 shares of Skeena Gold & Silver (TSX, NYSE: SKE), which is developing the Eskay Creek gold-silver project in British Columbia. The $8.9-million stake brought the four gold holdings to 3.1% of the September total.
The family office also increased its holding of Argentine oil and gas producer YPF (NYSE: YPF) by 13% to about 3.5 million American depositary shares worth $177.6 million. Genetic testing company Natera (Nasdaq: NTRA) remained its largest disclosed holding at 29% of the total.
Two other managers added to individual gold stocks. Sprott (TSX, NYSE: SII) increased its Barrick stake by 49% to 1.3 million shares. Tudor Investment more than doubled its Newmont common shares to 739,545 from 318,054. Tudor also held Newmont put options covering 250,400 shares and calls on 21,000 shares.
Duquesne listed 65 entries at Sept. 30, down from 95 worth $5.2 billion at June 30. Form 13F gives a quarter-end snapshot. It omits short positions and trade prices, and values options using the underlying shares. Print

source_document.body:
United Parcel Service said Tuesday it has agreed to acquire Smartways Logistics, a provider of time-critical courier services for the healthcare sector in Australia and New Zealand, underscoring the extent to which healthcare logistics has become a key strategic growth area for the company.
The planned acquisition, which is expected to close in the first half of 2027, will give UPS ( NYSE: UPS ) better access to Oceania in the rapidly growing healthcare logistics market, while connecting Smartways customers to UPS’s global transportation network for end-to-end international shipping.
The company has reorganized its business to focus more on high- margin industry verticals with complex logistics needs. UPS has targeted healthcare as a priority growth area, with healthcare logistics projected to grow 6% per year as next-generation healthcare products become more personalized, time-sensitive, and more challenging to move without damage, while increasingly being delivered directly to patients at home. In the third quarter, healthcare revenue at UPS reached $3 billion for the third consecutive quarter, with a run rate for more than $12 billion in healthcare revenue this year.
Smartways is the latest in a series of targeted UPS Healthcare investments. In April 2025, UPS acquired Canada-based Andlauer Healthcare Group , a provider of cold chain logistics services for the healthcare industry. Earlier that year, the freight transportation giant bought Frigo-Trans and sister company BPL, which provide temperature-controlled warehousing and transportation in Europe for pharmaceutical and biotech companies. It also acquired Bomi and MNX.
UPS Healthcare has about 20 million square feet of pharma-certified warehouse space under management, including extensive temperature-controlled facilities. Services include inventory management, cold chain packaging and shipping, storage and fulfillment of medical devices, and lab and clinical trial logistics. In the past two years, UPS invested $48 million to open 27 refrigerated truck cross-dock facilities around the world to meet rising demand from pharmaceutical companies, medical labs and biotech companies for temperature-controlled transport and storage of sensitive products.
UPS said the Smartways deal is part of a broader effort to expand healthcare capabilities in Asia-Pacific. The company has also broader network investments to facilitate more trade flows through its network, including a significantly larger hub at Clark airport in the Philippines and an upgraded air terminal in Seoul, South Korea — both of which have more refrigerated warehouse space for temperature-sensitive pharmaceuticals.
Smartways, which has more than 350 drivers, primarily offers same-day or next-day transport of medical devices and equipment, life sciences products, clinical trials and radiopharmaceuticals for the healthcare industry in Australia and New Zealand. A core business is delivering express freight into hospitals on behalf of medical device and equipment suppliers in key medical verticals and also offers contract logistics to manage inventory and distribution.
Smartways is owned by private equity firm The Riverside Company. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but The Australian Financial Review on Sunday reported that UPS had offered A$600 million, equivalent to $405 million.

Hub Group announced Tuesday that Nasdaq has given it until the end of the year to submit its delayed financial filings. Its shares will continue to trade on the exchange in the interim.
Hub Group ( NASDAQ: HUBG ) submitted a plan to regain compliance at an Oct. 27 hearing. It also asked Nasdaq to stay the delisting action .
Regaining compliance requires filing its delinquent annual report for last year and quarterly reports for the first three quarters of 2026. The delays stem from an accounting error it discovered in February. The company is also restating results stretching as far back as 2023.
“The Company’s finance and accounting team continues to work expeditiously to complete the restatement process and file the Delinquent Filings,” a news release stated. “However, the Company cannot confirm that it will be able to complete all of the Delinquent Filings before December 31, 2026.”
Hub Group said it would request another extension if it can’t meet the Dec. 31 deadline, but that a Nasdaq hearings panel has said it only has the authority to grant an extension to Mar. 12.
Early last month, Hub announced an overhaul of its board of directors , which included removing three directors and prompting the resignation of three others. The action included the appointment of four new members, including former CFO Thomas White.
Shares of HUBG are off 43% year-to-date compared to the S&P 500, which is up 7%.
Why it matters? A potential delisting highlights the severe operational and financial scrutiny Hub Group faces as it works to rectify an accounting error. Successfully filing its financials and completing the restatements are critical for maintaining investor confidence and preserving its public listing status.

source_document.body:
Photo: Jupiter
Old solar panels have silver and copper worth recovering. A new US recycling company called Jupiter plans to send metals recovered from retired solar panels and data center hardware to Korea Zinc’s refineries, including a $7.4 billion plant planned for Clarksville, Tennessee.
Solarcycle + PedalPoint Recycling = Jupiter
Jupiter joins US solar panel recycler Solarcycle and PedalPoint Recycling, Korea Zinc’s US recycling and metals business, into a single, fully integrated company. Jupiter says it’s launching with eight certified US facilities, nearly 1 million square feet of processing space, and about 250 employees. It’s also taking on customers from both businesses, including Microsoft, Prologis, and Brookfield.
For a solar farm or data center operator, that means a single company can take equipment out of service, resell parts with remaining useful life, and recycle the rest. Customers can track where the materials go and bring them back into their own supply chains.
Korea Zinc will hold a majority stake. Solarcycle’s Suvi Sharma will lead Jupiter as CEO, and PedalPoint’s Kevin Hahm will be CFO. Microsoft and Prologis Ventures are among Solarcycle’s existing investors.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
From a Georgia recycler to a Tennessee refinery
As Electrek reported in January , Solarcycle’s Cedartown, Georgia, plant was processing thousands of old solar panels a week when it opened. Solarcycle said the plant could handle up to 5 gigawatts’ worth of panels annually at full capacity, recovering materials such as glass, aluminum, copper, and silver.
The Tennessee plant adds a US refining step. Korea Zinc is developing the facility, called Project Crucible, with US government backing. It expects to start production in phases in 2029. The plant is designed to process about 1.1 million tons of raw materials per year and produce roughly 540,000 tons of finished products.

Owner Bought This 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air Nomad in 2023, Drove 200 Miles, Is Getting Rid of It
24 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
Scrap everything you knew about the 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air Nomad. It’s no longer valid. This restomod has made efforts to keep its stock appearance but has undergone an extensive mechanical transformation. However, the owner listed it for sale. He drove 200 miles in three years and probably realized he didn’t actually need it.
The 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air Nomad wears the bold Matador Red and contrasting India Ivory over a red and black interior, making it look like it rolled off the production line 69 years ago, featuring the perfect spec. It is not the “perfect spec” that sent the owner to Cars and Bids to list it for sale. It is most likely the fact that he doesn’t really need it. It is not exactly the ideal commute car or the one you would normally take on a road trip across the country.
The nearly seven-decade-old Chevy Bel Air Nomad is not all show and no go. The vehicle is powered by a Chevrolet Performance crate 350-cubic-inch V8, sporting a FiTeech throttle body fuel injection. The listing doesn’t reveal how much the 350 makes.
Chevrolet did not offer a 350-cubic-inch engine in 1957. The largest factory engine available in the 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air Nomad was the newly introduced 283-cubic-inch small-block V8, while the 350ci V8 did not debut until ten years later in 1967, starting in the Chevrolet Camaro.
Photo: Cars and Bids The restoration experts repolished the chrome exterior trim, replaced the rubber, checked the window seals, and replaced the seat foam. The car also needed to have its floor pans refinished in factory-style red oxide paint.
A GM 700R4 four-speed automatic transmission puts the power down through the rear wheels. The car sits on a Ford 9-inch rear end with a 3.73:1 final drive ratio. Power brakes with front-disc conversion provide the stopping power. Power steering and an upgraded suspension with front and rear sway bars are also part of the plan.
A factory-style Wonder Bar AM radio with Bluetooth integration made its way into the cabin where occupants sit in perfect comfort regardless of the weather, due to the Vintage Air air conditioning system.
Power windows, a power-adjustable front bench seat, and an aftermarket front center armrest with cupholders are also on board, along with retrofitted lap belts to keep the occupants secured in place.
Photo: Cars and Bids This is what the owner is now getting rid of, but is not willing to let it go without a fight. That is because the Bel Air Nomad stands as the rarest and most sought-after model of the iconic Tri-Five Chevrolet era between 1955 and 1957.
In the day, it came with the utility of a station wagon, the sleek, pillarless styling of a two-door coupe, and the larger tailfins, along with the 14-inch wheels. 1957 marked the final year for the original two-door Nomad body style, and hopefully, the seller knows how rare it is.
The five-digit odometer shows it has traveled 12,132 miles (19,525 kilometers). The seller drove only 200 of those, which means the Chevy Bel Air Nomad has been a garage queen for the past three years and, actually, for its entire life.
For the 1957 model year, Chevrolet built 6,103 domestic units (or 6,534 when including export and knock-down kits), making 1957 the rarest year of the original two-door Nomad. The Nomad accounted for less than 0.5% of the total production in 1955 and 1957.
Photo: Cars and Bids Starting at $2,571 in 1955 and rising to $2,857 in 1957 ($32,378 and $34,316, respectively), the Nomad was the most expensive model in the Bel Air lineup, costing more than even the Bel Air convertible.
On the current collector market, a 1957 Chevrolet Bel Air Nomad sells between $60,000 and $90,000 for a solid, driver-quality car, while freshly restored examples and high-end restomods like this one routinely trade for $100,000 to $150,000+.
With three days to go, the most generous offer on Cars and Bids sits at $25,000. Well, he surely needs a bit of optimism and patience to see how far it goes at the end of the auction.

Photo: Kolesa
Do you remember the new BMW Alpina 7 Series that we first encountered at the end of last month (October 2026)? Why, of course you do, because such a thing is not easily forgotten.
Subsequent to it being scooped in the open, it was sent to the Nardo racetrack in Italy for more testing, where it managed to reach 186 mph (300 kph). Keep in mind that it wasn’t built for speed but comfort, yet it certainly features a big dose of sportiness. After all, it’s an Alpina, and for decades, these models have been able to mix the sporty driving credentials with the comfort-oriented ones perfectly, while adding a big dose of novelties both inside and out.
Therefore, the upcoming BMW Alpina 7 Series will continue to do so, just like the previous-generation B7, and if you are wondering why it won’t be christened the Alpina B7, it is because the company is now part of the BMW Group. As for the family that founded Alpina, it is back in business under the Bovensiepen name . And they have quite a couple new products in their lineup, which follow a similar theme, including the 05 GT, based on the BMW M5 Touring, and the Spider, building on the Z4.
Now, while BMW Alpina is fine-tuning the new 7 Series in different environments, the pixel-altering crowd has started removing the camouflage on the car’s body using photo-editing software. One of the first rendering takes on this model that has crossed our screens came from Kolesa. The CGI’s shared in the gallery were the work of Nikita Chuyko, and they are very realistic, as they were based on the actual scoops mentioned above, and the car is sprinkled with the usual Alpina goodies.
Photo: Kolesa Compared to the latest BMW 7 Series , the Alpina variant features a new bumper at the front with redesigned vents on the sides and a new air intake in the middle that is narrower but taller. The integrated splitter is another novelty, and so are the yellow daytime running lights that will probably not be a thing. And if they are, then we have yet to see them on a prototype. Spy shots have revealed that the grille should feature a different pattern, though for what it’s worth, it carries over from the regular 7er on this CGI model.
The changes continue at the rear, where the vehicle sports a new bumper with vertical instead of horizontal reflectors that now sit further up. The diffuser is also more aggressive than the one equipping the regular BMW 7 Series, and has cutouts for four exhaust tips. A pair of pinstripe-like lines decorate the car’s profile, stretching from the front fenders to the taillights, and displaying Alpina’s name on them.
This rendered BMW Alpina 7 Series has a green paint finish on the outside, typical of other Alpina models, and rides on the sought-after wheels with their V-spoke pattern, which are much larger than the ones equipping the standard 7er. The imagined car also has a slightly lower ground clearance for faster cornering, and it displays its name in the middle of the splitter, and on the left-hand side of the trunk lid.
Photo: Kolesa Its interior has yet to open up to the camera, but expect the same Panoramic iDrive, free-floating infotainment system, and passenger display as the latest BMW 7 Series. However, we believe that new submenus and load screens will be part of the Alpina makeover alongside a new steering wheel, and different trim and upholstery, as well as perhaps exclusive treadplates, among other things.
BMW has already confirmed that the upcoming Alpina 7 Series will feature a V8 engine, and it is likely the unit powering the new M760 xDrive. The automaker hasn’t revealed the full specs, but it did confirm that the mill, which is a twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8, will produce approximately 570 hp, which is a bit more than the old 760i that had 563 hp on tap. If anything, the lump should produce more oomph in the new Alpina, and over 600 horsepower seems very likely, this writer believes.
The BMW Alpina 7 Series will sit at the very top of the latest 7er lineup, and it is expected to arrive in the United States of America for the 2028 model year. Thus, there may not be an M7, but the Alpina will definitely fill this void, combining plenty of oomph, sporty driving credentials, exclusive looks, and a comfortable ride like a real champ.
By the way, the 7er won’t be the only modern Bimmer that will get the Alpina treatment, as so will the next-generation X7 that is now in the making. But what’s your take on the design of the BMW Alpina 7 Series, as it was imagined by the quoted rendering artist? Do you fancy the look?

One-Off 1977 Jeep J10 Extended Cab Prototype Is Up for Auction for the First Time
20 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Jeep introduced its first pickup truck in 1947. Called the Willys Jeep Truck, it was joined by the Jeep Forward Control in 1956. Both were discontinued after the introduction of the more iconic Gladiator in 1962.
Originally launched under Willys Motors, the Gladiator was produced and sold as a Kaiser-Jeep vehicle between 1963 and 1970. The pickup truck soldiered on through AMC and Chrysler ownerships before it was discontinued after the 1988 model year.
In 1971, one year after Jeep was purchased by American Motors, the Gladiator name was dropped, and the truck became known as the Pickup or J-Series. The vehicles were designated as J2000 and J4000 from 1971 until 1973 and then as J10 and J20 through 1988. The 1977 pickup you see here is a J10, but it's not the average Jeep truck that rolled off the assembly line that year.
How so? Well, this J10 has an extended cab layout. And while it may seem like a regular production model, Jeep never offered such a version of the Gladiator . Despite its long production run of 27 years, the Gladiator was only offered as a regular cab pickup truck.
So what's the deal with this J10? Well, it was actually built by Jeep, but it never made it past the prototype stage. Built on a Wagoneer frame and a Cherokee Chief cab with second-row seating, the vehicle was put together to explore the potential of an extended cab version. The idea wasn't entirely new; Dodge launched an extended cab truck in 1973, while Ford joined the niche in 1974.
The concept wasn't entirely new for the platform either. Kaiser Argentina (IKA) built an extended cab variant of the truck for South American markets between 1963 and 1978. The local market also got a four-door double cab iteration. Neither made it to the United States.
Like most prototypes of the era, this J10 was intended to be crushed. Luckily, the man who supervised the project, Harold "Pete" Johnson (the chief of AMC/Jeep R&D), decided to store it in a back room of the Toledo plant. When he retired a few years later, Johnson was allowed to purchase the truck for $1.
The vehicle has remained in the care of Johnson and his family ever since, getting an extensive nut-and-bolt restoration to original specs. It was refinished in the correct Golden Ginger Poly paint and retains the custom-built passenger seat that leans forward to ease access to the rear seats.
The Jeep spent most of its life in storage but was exhibited at the Toledo Jeep Fest, the Bantam Jeep Heritage Festival, and at the AkzoNobel booth at the SEMA Show. It's been nearly 50 years since it rolled out of Jeep's Toledo facility, and the pickup truck is up for sale for the very first time.
The prototype will go under the hammer at Mecum's Kissimmee 2027 auction on January 8. It's impossible to tell how much it will fetch, but there's a chance that it will become one of the most expensive vintage Gladiators ever auctioned. As of this writing, the record is held by a 1979 J10 Honcho that sold for $58,300.

Confirmed: All-New Hyundai Elantra Coming to the U.S.
18 photos
Photo: Hyundai
Hyundai is expanding its presence in the United States with a $26 billion investment and 58 new or refreshed North American models scheduled through 2030. One of them is the new Elantra, which comes to revive the affordable sedan segment. The roadmap also includes 22 models from its luxury sister brand, Genesis.
As a matter of fact, several major model reveals and arrivals on the market are confirmed for the immediate future: the 2027 Hyundai Elantra and the 2028 Elantra Hybrid are part of the plan. The next-generation compact sedan makes its U.S. debut at AutoMobility LA on Thursday, November 19, 2026.
The model features sharper styling, as we have seen on the model sold in South Korea as the Avante , a more spacious cabin, and Hyundai's new Android-based Pleos Connect infotainment system with the Gleo AI assistant. The gas version arrives as a 2027 model, followed by the 2028 Hyundai Elantra Hybrid.
The automaker has yet to announce official U.S. pricing for the redesigned 2027 Elantra or 2028 Elantra Hybrid, but it is expected to arrive at under $30,000 in an attempt to steal market share from the Toyota Corolla and Corolla Hybrid or Honda Civic and Civic Hybrid.
Photo: Hyundai The Toyota Corolla, which starts at $24,620 ($26,470 for the Corolla Hybrid) is America's best-selling sedan with 217,905 units sold from January through October 2026. Honda Civic is keeping up with its, with 213,095 units moved this year to date.
The Civic starts at $26,290 for the base LX, while the Civic Hybrid is a $30,990 deal. That is where the all-new Elantra and Elantra Hybrid have to fall in order to stay competitive in an market that these models won't let die. Hyundai sold 140,614 Elantras from January to October in the United States.
Hyundai Ioniq 6 N is on its way to the U.S. Hyundai has also confirmed to Cars.com that the Hyundai Ioniq 6 N will arrive in America in the spring of 2027 in limited numbers. Hyundai doesn't say how many but says the model will have "extremely limited availability" at select dealerships. Pricing details will be disclosed closer to market launch date. The high-performance Ioniq 6 N the sole version of the Ioniq 6 offered in the U.S. for 2027, but customers have no reason to complain.
The high-performance sedan with zero tailpipe emissions is powered by a dual-motor setup, operating in an all-wheel-drive layout. The system produces 641 horsepower (650 metric horsepower) along with 568 pound-feet (568 Newton meters) of torque with the N Grin mode on. That is enough to make the sedan run from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 3.2 seconds with N Launch Control and all the way to 159 mph (257 kph).
Photo: Hyundai A lithium-ion battery pack with a capacity of 84.0 kWh (about 80.0 kWh usable) stores enough energy to make the Ioniq 6 N drive as far as 245 miles (394 kilometers) before it needs to be plugged in again, as rated by the EPA. Chassis reinforcements, larger brakes, upgraded cooling hardware, and the battery pack push the sedan's curb weight to roughly 4,775 pounds (2,166 kilograms).
The 2027 Hyundai Tucson and Tucson Hybrid are already listed on the official Hyundai USA site for an early 2027 arrival. The redesigned SUV introduces a next-generation powertrain, integrating either the 1.6-liter turbocharged inline-four with zero electric assistance or the same engine assisted by a dual-motor setup and a 1.49-kWh lithium-ion battery.
Expectedly, the hybrid variant will sit at the top of the lineup with 233 horsepower and 280 pound-feet (380 Newton meters) of torque, put down through either the front wheels or all four corners with the help of the HTRAC AWD system. The all-new Tucson also gets the new Pleos Connect and a rugged XRT PRO trim.
Starting in 2027, Hyundai plans to introduce its first extended-range electric vehicles, including an upcoming Santa Fe EREV, estimated to be capable of over 600 miles (966 kilometers) of total range.
Massive investment in U.S. production As part of its 2030 roadmap, Hyundai has also confirmed plans to enter new North American segments with a midsize body-on-frame pickup truck, which would give the Ford Ranger and the Toyota Tacoma a run for their money, along with a large commercial van.
To support its North American lineup and avoid tariffs imposed on imported goods, Hyundai is investing $26 billion in the United States. The move is expected to create 25,000 direct jobs and add 500,000 units of production capacity at the brand’s plants in Montgomery, Alabama, Ellabell, Georgia, and Donaldsonville, Louisiana.
While Hyundai is expanding the Metaplant in Georgia to produce hybrids and EVs, alongside a $12.6 billion battery joint venture, nearly $500 million is invested in Montgomery to build engines for the next-gen Tucson and Santa Fe, as well as Hyundai’s first extended-range EVs.
Hyundai will also build a $5.8 billion low-carbon steel mill in Louisiana to supply its auto plants in the United States.

source_document.body:
Hyundai revealed the production-ready Neira EV for the first time, a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV set to launch in Indonesia on November 20.
Hyundai prepares to launch the 7-seat Neira EV
After introducing the Neira Concept at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS) in July, Hyundai is gearing up to open pre-orders on November 20.
The Neira is a pretty “big” deal as Hyundai’s first locally produced seven-seat electric SUV in Indonesia.
Ahead of its official debut on Friday at GAIKINDO Auto Week (GAW) 2026, Hyundai offered a closer look at the upcoming Neira.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The electric SUV is essentially a Hyundai-badged version of the Kia Carens Clavis EV that launched last year. Aside from the Hyundai logos, a few minor tweaks to the front and rear ends, and new wheels and headlights, it’s a near replica.
Inside, both are equipped with dual 12.3″ instrument display and center navigation screens, plus an added climate control panel.
Hyundai Neira seven-seat electric SUV (Source: Hyundai Indonesia)
Hyundai didn’t reveal battery or powertrain specs, but the Neira is expected to use the same 42 kWh and 51.4 kWh battery packs as the Carens Clavis EV. The former offers an MIDC range of up to 251 mi (404 km), while the latter has up to 304 mi (490 km) on a single charge.
Both batteries can be charged from 10% to 80% in around 39 minutes using a 100 kW DC fast charger.
The Kia Carens Clavis is 4,550 mm long, 1,800 mm wide, and 1,708 mm tall, with a 2,780 mm wheelbase, so Hyundai’s Neira will likely be about the same size, if not slightly bigger.
Hyundai said the Neira has four key advantages: A higher ground clearance, Hyundai Bluelink connectivity tech, a Blind-spot View Monitor (BVM), and easy third-row access.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by Hyundai Motors Indonesia (@hyundaimotorindonesia)
Ahead of its upcoming launch, Hyundai is taking the electric 7-seater on a trip to prove its capabilities, going from Kilometer Nol in Banda Aceh to Banda Neira, which is about 4,000 kilometers (about 2,500 miles).
While Hyundai may export the Neira EV to overseas markets like India, don’t expect it to reach the US.
Hyundai already sells a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV, the IONIQ 9 , which is built at Hyundai’s Metaplant in Georgia.
